comments.text: I have personal experience in this. When I was a police officer I got called out to a cross burning in a middle class neighborhood. I met with the victim and sure enough, there was a charred cross on his lawn. I took a report and did what I always do when I didn't have calls holding. I went and talked to the neighbors. The neighbor across the street told me he saw everything. The owner of the house did it. He also told me he would testify in court. I went back over to the "victims" house and when he answered the door I told him, "Don't say anything until I'm finished." I then read him his rights and told him "We prosecute for filing a false police report. One of your neighbors is willing to swear out a statement saying you did it. This is your one chance to tell me the truth." He broke down and admitted he did it to "Bring attention to all the racism in the neighborhood."
